Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan have so far dominated this tour. Their team in the shorter formats seems to be a changed side with victory following them wherever they go. The Windies batsmen have been unable to tackle the spinners and not really come to terms with the bat. The 2nd ODI of the series will be held in Sharjah on the 2nd of October at 1630 IST. Will the visitors be able to finally answer the spinners or will Pakistan clinch the ODI series as well? Join us as we cover the action. Until then, goodbye and take care!

AZHAR ALI first of all thanks the Almighty. He says that it was a wonderful team effort and that it was a much needed victory. Adds that his team is still carrying the momentum from their recent wins. (On their batting) Says that the ball wasn't coming on to the bat too well but Sarfraz Ahmed and Babar Azam batted quite well and that it was a wonderful team effort. Opines that their side are now batting deep with a couple of more all-rounders. Adds that their fielding and fitness have improved and that they are improving step-by-step and moving forward. States that the youngsters are vital for the limited overs side as they are taking over in the shorter formats by bringing their energy and attitude into the game. Adds that they have to come in with the right attitude and, God willing, keep doing the same. (On it being a must-win season) He says that they are focusing on improving themselves and looking to play good cricket. Adds that the entire coaching staff is working on it and the players are looking to improve their weaker points as they want to keep winning matches and improve their standing too.

JASON HOLDER feels they didn't do well today. Adds they kept losing wickets at regular intervals and that's not a good sign. Further says unlike Pakistan, they failed to rotate the strike and build the momentum. States they will be looking to do well in the coming matches. On the bowling, he says he is happy with the overall efforts and it were the spinners that pulled the game back in the first innings. On the wicket, he says it was a lovely pitch which had something for everyone.

MAN OF THE MATCH, BABAR AZAM says he is really happy and wants to thank the Almighty for letting him win the match for his side. Adds his plan was to bat as long as possible. Further says Sarfraz helped him cool down in the middle overs and he just wants to continue the hard work in the future.

Earlier in the day, Pakistan set a decent total of 284 runs, thanks to a power-packed performance by Babar Azam who scored 120. The rest of the batsmen batted well too, with some good partnerships formed. The West Indies bowlers gave it their best but were not able to stem the steady flow of runs thereby suffering a loss in the series opener.

Pakistan's bowlers looked in control throughout. They limited the scoring to a crawl and whenever the visitors looked to relax, a wicket fell. Despite an achievable target, the pressure never seemed to be on their shoulders. Today was Mohammad Nawaz's day as he picked up 4 scalps, just missing out on his fifth, and gave away just a handful of runs. The other bowlers were equally effective though. The exception was Shoaib Malik, who failed to pick up a wicket and had an economy rate higher than the others.

That's the end for West Indies as Pakistan take a 1-0 lead in the ODI series. The tourists will surely be disappointed by the contest that was reminiscent of the recently concluded T20I series. They had to struggle for runs with their leading scorer being Marlon Samuels with 46 runs. None of their batsmen could ever really settle in and they could never really get a decent partnership going. Marlon Samuels hung around the longest but he couldn't find any support from the other batsmen. Towards the end, Carlos Brathwaite and Sunil Narine made useful cameos but were soon sent walking back. Their tailenders had fun in the middle but it was just a matter of time before they were dismissed.
